Build the storey-by-storey building envelope of every site

Source: R/envelope.R
build_envelopes.Rd

The core of the engine: a stack of storey footprints per site, each the site's buildable ground clipped back from every boundary by every rule that applies at that storey's height, then capped by coverage, landscaping and floorplate limits.

Usage

build_envelopes(
  x,
  rulebook = NULL,
  variant_choice = NULL,
  include_density = FALSE,
  keep_geometry = FALSE,
  keep_setbacks = FALSE,
  baseline = NULL,
  max_storeys = 60,
  height_add = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A scenario(), or sites from prepare_sites() (then give rulebook).

rulebook

The rulebook, when x is prepared sites.

variant_choice

Overrides the rulebook's variant_choice.

include_density

Also build envelopes for density-method zones.

keep_geometry

Keep each storey's footprint polygon.

keep_setbacks

Keep, for every boundary at every storey, the setback applied and the rule (and citation) that set it. One row per boundary per storey, so meant for a few sites, not a region.

baseline

An earlier plancap_envelope to copy unchanged sites from.

max_storeys

Guard against a runaway height (not a plan rule).

height_add

Optional named numeric vector, by site id: metres of extra height (as a height bonus gives), added to total and occupiable height.

Value

A plancap_envelope: a list with stack (one row per site and storey of the chosen variant), sites (one row per site: variant, storeys, height reached, footprint, floor area, the constraint that bound most), variants (every variant's total, per site), optional geometry and setbacks, a report and the per-site signatures.

Method

Carried over from capacityengine, where each choice was tested:

  • Loop over storeys, vectorise over sites. At each storey every live site is handled in one set of GEOS calls.

  • One setback per boundary per storey. Yards, recession planes, upper-level and proportional setbacks all say "at this height, stand this far back from this boundary", so the binding distance on a boundary is the largest any applicable rule asks, and the clip is a single buffer at that distance.

  • A storey is tested at its ceiling (level_reference = "ceiling"): the whole storey must fit under a plane.

  • A zone's storey height is its own (stated height over stated storeys), and does not change when an overlay changes the site's height.

  • Coverage and landscaping are shares of net site area, not of the clipped envelope, and the most restrictive applies (PLAN 3.5).

  • The stack never widens going up, and a storey smaller than the minimum floorplate ends it.

  • Reflex corners are filled with wedges, so a bend in a boundary away from the site leaves no hairline teeth; parts smaller than a floorplate are dropped.

  • Alternative standards are evaluated separately and each site takes the most enabling (variant_choice = "max"), or as the rulebook says.

A rule whose condition cannot be evaluated is not guessed at: a positive trigger (adjacent_zones, facing, a road width) is not applied, which overstates; an exemption (not_adjacent_zones) is not applied, so the rule bites, which understates. Both are counted in the run report.

Water yards (setbacks naming riparian, coastal or lakeside) are measured from the water features themselves, and the land within reach is taken off the buildable ground.

Incremental runs

Each site's result carries a signature of everything that determines it: its geometry and boundaries, its effective rules and the run settings. Given a baseline envelope, sites whose signature is unchanged are copied from it rather than recomputed, so a plan change that touches a tenth of the sites costs about a tenth of a run. The result is identical to a full run.

Examples

town <- exampleton()
sc <- scenario("Operative", rulebook_example("exampleton"),
  parcels = town$parcels[town$parcels$parcel_type == "land", ][1:60, ],
  roads = town$parcels[town$parcels$parcel_type == "road", ],
  zoning = town$zoning, layers = town["height_areas"])
env <- build_envelopes(sc)
env
#> <plancap envelope> Operative: 60 of 60 sites build; 80,511 m2 of floor area.
#> Plan-enabled, gross, blank-slate building envelope (before yield and use
#> split).
#> Binding constraint by storey: coverage 68%, geometry 32%.
